title: Plan R1009 and R1012: the zero-duration shape rule and the coverage guard
body:
Two steward plans under `docs/plans/oracle/`. No code.

**`zero-duration-listing-shape`** implements **OD-14 / R1009** (evidence
BL-15). The index warning judges each listing entry on its own evidence
instead of counting: no duration AND no date is the flat listing's Shorts
shape and reports as a one-line count; a real date with no duration is the
silent-drop shape and keeps the banner, at any count. The "more than one"
threshold goes. BL-15's eight measured ids become the regression, paired with
a ninth dated entry that must still fire.

**`transcript-coverage-guard`** implements **OD-23 / R1012** (evidence BL-27).
`Selection` carries `has_transcript`, written where `select_all` already
distinguishes a cache hit from the empty stand-in it substitutes. Both stages
print coverage on every run, and zero coverage over a non-empty population
refuses naming `fetch` rather than printing a zero-token projection under R7's
stop sentence.

Neither plan files an uncertainty — every decision derives from the design, and
the ones that came closest to the line carry their derivation rather than an
assertion.

**Ordering.** `transcript-coverage-guard` is built before the selection and
excerpting work it guards: every later measurement in this milestone, including
R8's calibration factor, is taken from a run whose coverage it reports.

Carries a merge of the base branch so the required checks run against the tree
this will land on.
